title: Common small refinements of filtered presentations
statement: Use universes, nerves, coherent diagrams, colimits, filteredness and compactness from [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] and [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal E$ be a locally small infinity category admitting all small filtered colimits, and let $\kappa$ be an uncountable regular cardinal in the smaller universe. Let $A_0,A_1$ be small $\kappa$-filtered partially ordered sets and let $p_i:N(A_i)\to\mathcal E$ be diagrams taking values in $\kappa$-compact objects and having equivalent colimits. Given subsets $T_i\subseteq A_i$ with $|T_i|<\kappa$, there exist subsets $B_i\subseteq A_i$ with $|B_i|<\kappa$ that contain $T_i$, are filtered (every finite subset has an upper bound, including the empty subset), and satisfy $\operatorname{colim}_{N(B_0)}p_0|_{N(B_0)}\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{N(B_1)}p_1|_{N(B_1)}$. The equivalence is between these two restricted colimits; neither is asserted to equal the original total colimit.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.13, printed pp. 478-480; the source explicitly requires both diagrams to take values in the full subcategory of κ-compact objects.

proof.text: First compare the two cocone models used here. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus] to the opposite target and opposite indexing simplicial set, using the opposite-category and cone identities in clause (4) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence]. This gives the right-cone comparison between join-shaped cocones and the coherent-transformation cocones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], with the boundary diagram and apex fixed. Here a join cocone $\bar d:K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal E$ is called colimiting when its induced coherent cocone, obtained by precomposition with the map $K\times\Delta^1\to K^{\triangleright}$ that keeps the initial $K$-vertices of each interval simplex and sends its final vertices to the cone vertex, is colimiting in the sense of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]; this map is the opposite of the comparison of [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus], and it is natural in $K$, so restricting a join cocone along $L^{\triangleright}\to K^{\triangleright}$ restricts its induced coherent cocone along $L\to K$. Equivalence of the resulting cocone categories preserves initial objects: the quasi-inverse identifies the mapping spaces into any other cocone, so their contractibility is unchanged.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.13, p. 479, common apex and initial recursive diagram

proof.text: Choose a colimit object $c$ of $p_0$ and an equivalence from a colimit object of $p_1$ to $c$. Composing the latter cocone with this equivalence gives a cocone with apex $c$; composition with its inverse gives the inverse comparison of the relevant mapping spaces, so it is still colimiting. By the fixed-boundary, fixed-apex join comparison, choose colimiting join cocones $\bar p_i:N(A_i)^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal E$ with this same apex $c$. All occurrences of $T_0,T_1$ and of the integers below are disjoint labelled copies. Put $D=N(T_0)\amalg N(T_1)$, and put $K_n=D\star N(\{0,\ldots,n-1\})$ for $n\geq0$. Using the right-cone comparison of Step 1, at $n=0$ the two restricted join cocones glue to $\bar q_0:D^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal E$, since their only overlap is the vertex $c$. Here and below joins and cones are the degreewise constructions of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone].

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.13, p. 479, common apex and initial recursive diagram

proof.text: The induction will choose $a_n\in A_i$ when $i\equiv n\pmod2$ and maps $\bar q_n:K_n^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal E$ with apex $c$, each restricting to the preceding map. For each $i=0,1$, the elements $a_j$ of parity $i$ are nondecreasing and dominate every member of $T_i$. Write $K'_{i,n}=N(T_i)\star N(\{j<n:j\equiv i\pmod2\})\subseteq K_n$. Require that the restriction of $\bar q_n$ to $(K'_{i,n})^{\triangleright}$ be the pullback of $\bar p_i$ under the map sending $t\in T_i$ to itself, $j$ to $a_j$, and the cone vertex to the cone vertex. This is a monotone map even if some $a_j$ repeat. Every vertex of $q_n=\bar q_n|_{K_n}$ is then a value of $p_0$ or $p_1$, hence is $\kappa$-compact. Also $K_n$ is $\kappa$-small: nondegenerate simplices of $N(T_i)$ are finite chains, so their number is at most $\max(|T_i|,\aleph_0)<\kappa$; taking a disjoint union and joining a finite nerve retains this bound. The base map from Step 2 satisfies the invariant with no selected indices.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.13, p. 479, recursive invariant and compact-diagram hypotheses

proof.text: For the step from $n$ to $n+1$, put $i\equiv n\pmod2$, let $S_{i,n}=T_i\cup\{a_j:j<n,\ j\equiv i\pmod2\}$, and let $I_{i,n}=\{a\in A_i:s\leq a\text{ for all }s\in S_{i,n}\}$. This set is nonempty and $\kappa$-filtered: for any fewer than $\kappa$ members of $I_{i,n}$, their union with $S_{i,n}$ still has cardinality less than $\kappa$, and an upper bound in $A_i$ lies in $I_{i,n}$. This includes the empty family. To see the nerve is $\kappa$-filtered in the simplicial definition, take a $\kappa$-small diagram into it and choose an upper bound for all its vertex images; the order arrows from those images to the bound define its cone, with all simplices compatible because a poset nerve has unique simplices on any specified chain. Its inclusion in $A_i$ is upward cofinal, since $S_{i,n}\cup\{a\}$ has an upper bound for every $a\in A_i$.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.13, p. 479, the upper-bound tail A_i(n); cofinality made explicit

proof.text: Write $\iota:I_{i,n}\to A_i$ for this inclusion. Its nerve is final in the sense of [lem-coef-infinity-cofinality-space-test], by criterion (3) there, which for the nerve of an ordinary functor is weak contractibility of the nerves of the ordinary comma categories. For $b\in A_i$ the comma category $(b\downarrow\iota)$ has as objects the $a\in I_{i,n}$ with $b\leq a$, the arrow $b\to a$ being unique, so it is the subposet $\{a\in I_{i,n}:b\leq a\}$. It is nonempty because $S_{i,n}\cup\{b\}$ has an upper bound, and every finite subset of it has an upper bound in $I_{i,n}$, which again lies above $b$. By the nerve argument in Step 4, now for finite diagrams, its nerve is an $\aleph_0$-filtered quasicategory, hence weakly contractible by the filtered-contractibility clause of [lem-coef-infinity-coslice-colimit-formula]. Hence restriction along $N(\iota)$ carries colimiting coherent cocones to colimiting coherent cocones. By the naturality noted in Step 1, the induced coherent cocone of $\bar p_i|_{N(I_{i,n})^{\triangleright}}$ is the restriction along $N(\iota)$ of that of $\bar p_i$. The restricted join cocone $\bar p_i|_{N(I_{i,n})^{\triangleright}}$ is therefore still colimiting with apex $c$. The posets are small, and $\mathcal E$ has all their filtered colimits by hypothesis.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.13, p. 479, the upper-bound tail A_i(n); cofinality made explicit

proof.text: Let $K'=K'_{i,n}$ and $K=K_n$. There is a map $r:K'\star N(I_{i,n})^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal E$ obtained from $\bar p_i$: on $K'$ use the monotone map of Step 3, on $I_{i,n}$ use inclusion, and send the final vertex to the final vertex. This is defined on the whole join because every value of that monotone map is at most every member of $I_{i,n}$. Its restriction to $K'\star\{\infty\}$ agrees with $\bar q_n$ by the invariant. Apply [lem-coef-compact-relative-cocone-factorization] to $q_n$, $K'\subseteq K_n$, this $r$, $u=\bar q_n$, and the colimit cocone from Step 5. Its compactness and size hypotheses were checked in Step 3. Every small $\kappa$-filtered index is filtered, since finite simplicial sets are $\kappa$-small; thus the assumed small filtered colimits in $\mathcal E$ supply the small $\kappa$-filtered colimits required by that lemma. The tail is small, nonempty and $\kappa$-filtered by Step 4, and $\kappa$ is infinite regular by hypothesis. Obtain $a_n\in I_{i,n}$ and $v:K_n\star\Delta^1\to\mathcal E$ with all four prescribed restrictions. Rename the two vertices of $\Delta^1$ as $n,\infty$; this identifies its domain with $K_{n+1}^{\triangleright}$, and define $\bar q_{n+1}=v$. The restriction at $\infty$ is exactly $\bar q_n$, so no earlier simplex changes. The prescribed restriction on $K'\star\Delta^1$ is exactly the required $\bar p_i$-diagram on the enlarged parity subdiagram; the other parity subdiagram is unchanged. Finally $a_n\in I_{i,n}$ proves all new order inequalities in the invariant. This argument covers both even and odd $n$.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.13, pp. 479-480, relative cocone pullback and its incoming edge; both parities

proof.text: Take the union of the compatible maps $\bar q_n$. Each simplex of $(D\star N(\mathbf N))^{\triangleright}$ has finitely many integer vertices, so belongs to some $K_n^{\triangleright}$; compatibility gives a well-defined simplicial map $\bar q$ on this union. Let $q$ be its restriction to $N(\mathbf N)$, and put $B_i=T_i\cup\{a_j:j\equiv i\pmod2\}$. Each $B_i$ contains $T_i$ and has cardinality at most $|T_i|+\aleph_0<\kappa$, because $\kappa$ is uncountable. Each is nonempty and filtered: a finite set of selected elements is bounded by a sufficiently late selected element of the same parity, and that element also bounds every member of $T_i$. For the empty subset use $a_i$. These arguments also handle empty $T_i$, terminal $A_i$, and repeated selected elements.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.13, p. 479, the two countably enlarged subsets

proof.text: For $i=0,1$ let $H_i=\{j\in\mathbf N:j\equiv i\pmod2\}$ and let $P_i$ be the ordered sum of $T_i$ and $H_i$: retain their orders and put every element of $T_i$ below every element of $H_i$. The map $f_i:P_i\to B_i$, sending $t$ to $t$ and $j$ to $a_j$, is monotone and surjective, hence upward cofinal. All four posets $H_i,P_i,B_i,\mathbf N$ are small, nonempty and filtered; $P_i$ is filtered because a sufficiently late parity integer bounds any finite subset. The inclusions $H_i\to P_i$ and $H_i\to\mathbf N$ are upward cofinal as well.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.13, p. 479, comparison with the alternating sequential colimit; repeated indices handled by cofinal monotone maps

proof.text: For each of the three monotone maps $g:P\to Q$ used below, between nonempty filtered posets with every $b\in Q$ below some $g(a)$, the argument of Steps 4-5 applies: the comma category $(b\downarrow g)$ is the subposet $\{a\in P:b\leq g(a)\}$, nonempty by upward cofinality and with an upper bound in it for every finite subset, since an upper bound in $P$ of finitely many members still maps above $b$. Its nerve is $\aleph_0$-filtered, hence weakly contractible by [lem-coef-infinity-coslice-colimit-formula], so $N(g)$ is final by criterion (3) of [lem-coef-infinity-cofinality-space-test]. No injectivity of $g$ is used.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.13, p. 479, comparison with the alternating sequential colimit; repeated indices handled by cofinal monotone maps

proof.text:
The union invariant identifies the pullback of $p_i|_{N(B_i)}$ to $N(P_i)$ with $\bar q|_{N(P_i)}$ without its last cone vertex, and its restriction to $N(H_i)$ with $q|_{N(H_i)}$. Choose colimiting cocones of $p_i|_{N(B_i)}$ and of $q$; they exist by the assumed small filtered-colimit existence in $\mathcal E$. Restricting the first along $N(f_i)$ and then along $N(H_i)\to N(P_i)$ gives, by finality, colimiting cocones with the same apex on $p_iN(f_i)$ and on $q|_{N(H_i)}$; restricting the second along $N(H_i)\to N(\mathbf N)$ gives another colimiting cocone on $q|_{N(H_i)}$. Two colimiting cocones on one diagram are initial objects of its cocone category, so their apices are equivalent. This gives
$$\operatorname{colim}_{N(B_i)}p_i\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{N(P_i)}p_iN(f_i)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{N(H_i)}q\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{N(\mathbf N)}q.$$
Comparing the two values of $i$ gives the claimed equivalence of restricted colimits. The cocone to $c$ was used only for the recursion; it has not been asserted colimiting on either $B_i$.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.13, p. 479, comparison with the alternating sequential colimit; repeated indices handled by cofinal monotone maps
